sentences.text: Prophaethon was an extinct seabird that lived during the Early Eocene, approximately 56 to 49 million years ago.
Scientists classify this animal as a distant relative of modern tropicbirds.
The genus Prophaethon was first described by Andrews in 1899.

The type species, P. shrubsolei, is known from a holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consisting of a skull and some limb bones recovered from the London Clay on the Isle of Sheppey, England.
Gerald Mayr later described additional remains of P. shrubsolei and a second species, P. waltonensis, both found at Walton-on-the-Naze.
The parent group of the genus Prophaethon is Prophaethontidae, and the animal belongs to this family.
The time range for Prophaethon spans from the Thanetian to the Ypresian, between 59.24 and 48.07 million years ago.
